hints.title: Non-Square Transposition Obstacle
hints.text: Transposing a rectangular matrix of size M x N produces a new matrix of size N x M where rows become columns. How can index swapping populate the transposed matrix in a single pass?

hints.title: Coordinate Inversion Invariant
hints.text: For every cell at coordinate (r, c) in the original matrix, its destination in the transposed matrix is uniquely (c, r).

hints.title: Direct Grid Mapping Procedure
hints.text: Create a result matrix of dimension n x m with zeroes. Iterate row r from 0 to m - 1 and column c from 0 to n - 1, assigning res[c][r] = matrix[r][c]. Return res.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Every entry is copied directly to its inverted coordinate in O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: In-place non-square matrix transposition requires complex cyclic permutation permutation cycles.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Allocating the output grid consumes zero additional auxiliary storage.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Correct handling of dimension inversion from M x N to N x M.
